properties.areaDesc: City and Borough of Juneau
properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 16 at 4:49AM AKDT until October 17 at 1:30AM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Nuisance flooding on roadways and small stream flooding
caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Roadways within the Mendenhall Valley, areas around Montana
Creek and Jordan Creek.

* WHEN...Until 130 AM AKDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Ponding on roadways impacting the Friday morning commute. Some
low-water crossings may become impassable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 441 AM AKDT, satellite estimates indicate heavy rain ongoing
across the advisory area. Rapid river rises will cause nusiance
flooding of roadways, poor drainage areas, and small streams
reaching bankfull conditions, especially near Montana Creek And
Jordan Creek. Between 1.5 and 2.5 inches of rain has fallen in
the last 12 hours. The heaviest rainfall rates of 0.2 to 0.3
inches in 1 hour are expected through the next couple of hours
before quickly diminishing into Friday morning. Additional
rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are possible.
- For Jordan Creek near Juneau:
At 4:00am the stage was 8.3 feet.
Flood Stage is 9.7 feet.
Forecast: A crest around 9.2 feet is expected around 9:00am
Friday.

Impacts:
At 9.2 feet: This is the stage when Jordan Creek is at bankfull and
water will begin to inundate areas along the edges of the creek near
Race Reality and Jordan Square.
At 9.7 feet: Water will inundate the Jordan Square's front and back
parking lots, around Jordan Creek office condominiums with up to one
foot of water. Some residential driveways will be flooded and cut
off.

For Montana Creek at Back Loop Bridge:
At 12:00pm the stage was 11.2 feet.
Flood Stage is 14.5 feet.
Forecast: A crest around 14.5 feet is expected around 7:00am
Friday.

Impacts:
At 14.5 feet: Water begins flowing over the low water crossing on
Montana Creek Road. Bankfull conditions at the gauge with water
starting to inundate adjacent undeveloped fields along Mendenhall
Loop Road.
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

properties.areaDesc: Guam; Rota; Tinian; Saipan
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Watch issued October 16 at 10:48PM ChST until October 19 at 4:00AM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Warning, large, hazardous breaking
waves of 7 to 9 feet Saturday afternoon will become dangerous,
building to as high as 35 feet for Guam, 25 feet for Rota and 20
feet for Tinian and Saipan. For the Coastal Flood Watch,
significant coastal flooding possible.

* WHERE...For the High Surf Warning, initially east facing reefs
of Guam, Rota, Tinian, and Saipan; spreading to all reefs
through Sunday afternoon. The Coastal Flood Watch is also for
all reefs of the Marianas.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Warning, from 5 PM Saturday to 4 AM
ChST Monday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from Saturday
afternoon through late Sunday night.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
may be inundated. Some shoreline erosion may occur. Breaking
waves can sweep people off jetties and docks, and into dangerous
seas. Life-threatening swimming conditions and significant
beach erosion can be expected. Coastal inundation of 5 to 7 feet
for Guam, 2 to 4 feet for Rota and 1 to 3 feet for Tinian and
Saipan is possible along with coastal flooding and beach
erosion.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...As TS Champi approaches the Marianas, surf
conditions are expected to deteriorate rapidly, with surf
reaching 9 feet Saturday afternoon, building to dangerous/deadly
levels through Saturday night.
properties.instruction:
Everyone should remain out of the water due to life-threatening
surf conditions. Stay off of jetties, piers, and other waterside
infrastructure.

properties.description:
* WHAT...North winds 15 to 25 mph with gusts up to 40 mph expected.

* WHERE...Portions of south central and southwest Alabama, northwest
Florida, and southeast Mississippi.

* WHEN...From 10 PM this evening to 7 PM CDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Strong and gusty winds will be capable of downing
numerous additional compromised trees which would result in renewed
power outages in vulnerable areas impacted by the extreme winds
during Hurricane Isaias. In addition, large debris piles from storm
cleanup may be blown about resulting in additional hazards to
anyone nearby outdoors along with potentially blocking previously
cleared roadways. Additional road closures will be possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Many trees are leaning over power lines,
homes, and roads in the impacted area. Frequent wind gusts forecast
between 35 and 40 mph will create dangerous conditions outdoors in
the vulnerable areas. Elsewhere, winds may result in large tree
branches downed and localized power outages.
properties.instruction:
Use extreme caution if you must travel or be outdoors Friday night
through Saturday. Remain alert for potential falling trees and power
lines, blown debris, and additional damage to structures that remain
compromised from the hurricane.

around Ketchikan. Between 3 and 4.5 inches of rain have fallen in

additional rainfall amounts up to 1.0 inch expected.
